artifacts.description: Square steatite seal carved with the famous 'unicorn' motif and undeciphered Indus script. Used to stamp goods and mark ownership across Harappan trade networks.
artifacts.name: Indus Unicorn Seal

artifacts.description: Harappan seal depicting a mythological animal with pictographic symbols — typical of the thousands of seals found at Mohenjo-daro.
artifacts.name: Harappan Animal Seal

artifacts.description: Pair of Harappan seals with mythological animals, c. 2300 BCE. Small, finely carved, and pierced with a boss for suspension.
artifacts.name: Pair of Harappan Seals

artifacts.description: Modern terracotta seal in Harappan style (Molela clay art) — shows how Indus motifs survive in living craft traditions. Style reference only.
artifacts.name: Terracotta Seal in Harappan Style

artifacts.description: Bronze Shiva as Nataraja, Lord of Dance — the iconic Chola bronze cast by the lost-wax process. The ring of fire (prabhamandala) symbolises the cosmic cycle.
artifacts.name: Chola Bronze Nataraja
artifacts.source_note: Reference photo: Metropolitan Museum of Art collection

artifacts.description: Chola-period Nataraja surrounded by the prabhamandala ring of fire, standing on the dwarf of ignorance (Apasmara).
artifacts.name: Nataraja with Ring of Fire

artifacts.description: Shiva Nataraja in bronze, Chola period 11th century CE — slender tribhanga pose, typical of high-Chola casting at its peak.
artifacts.name: Chola Shiva Nataraja, 11th century

artifacts.description: Amphora in black-figure style (modern museum replica of c. 550–480 BCE): black silhouetted figures on the red Attic clay ground.
artifacts.name: Greek Black-Figure Amphora

artifacts.description: Greek vase in red-figure style (modern museum replica of c. 480–320 BCE): red figures reserved against a black gloss background.
artifacts.name: Greek Red-Figure Vase

artifacts.description: Diorite statue of Pharaoh Khafre (Chephren), builder of the Second Pyramid at Giza. The falcon Horus enfolds the king's head from behind.
artifacts.name: Diorite Statue of Khafre

artifacts.description: Clay tablet with circular map design and cuneiform (replica in Neo-Babylonian style, c. 700–500 BCE) — the world's earliest known world map tradition.
artifacts.name: Babylonian World-Map Tablet

artifacts.description: Rectangular clay tablet covered in wedge-shaped cuneiform script (replica in Old Babylonian style) — used for accounts, letters and literature.
artifacts.name: Cuneiform Clay Tablet

artifacts.description: Roman clay amphora from Pompeii, 1st century CE — the standard shipping jar of the Roman world for wine, oil and garum.
artifacts.name: Roman Amphora from Pompeii

artifacts.description: Roman transport vessel / shipwreck pottery, 1st–2nd century CE — coarse maritime ware recovered from ancient wreck sites.
artifacts.name: Roman Shipwreck Vessel
